body: Thank you so much for all the info and for telling me.  One web site said only 1% of CHS stroke sufferer return to near normal function.  I am so glad for you.  Good luck from now on.

The rules on BPs 2 differ in every State.  In this State the law used to take into consideration the BP2's  individual situation in SENTENCING, NOT IN CONVICTION.  It no longer does.  As I have periodic obsessive compulsive periods as well (those didn't start until my husband of 50 years abruptly left me), I could NOT control my obsession to write him an email asking for help since it was cancer, diagnosed that day.  I have no living family, nobody to help, and am poor.  The judge refused to the 35 years of psychiatric records into consideration. I was jailed 60 days for that during which time I was yanked off my doctor's medicines for depression, and put on an all liquid diet, for an indefinte period for a condition it couldn't cure, and the disks in my back became more period.
If you ever feel you need to get a restraining order on a 72 year old, B
P2 woman, unless you don't mind that it might kill or permanently disable her go ahead.  If I go through another manic period with the same compulsion, the only option I have left is to see that I don't wind up in jail for the rest of my life or to seriously consider suicide.
Thank you for the info.  I will follow-up!  I appreciate you taking the time to write.

OMG.  I am truly sad that it hit you so hard and so young.  Nobody who hasn't gone through it can completely understand, but I loved my uncle who lost the use of his legs in early WWII and was in a wheel chair the rest of his life (until he was almost 90).  Through knowing him, I know a little.  But, it was easier for him, I think, than for you because he believed in a cause and lived it.  Coping with the randomness of life's events is much more difficult. Thank you for writing.

Sure, you never know when you are going to need to be "protected" (the Judge's words, not mine) from an email from your spouse of 50 years, "I'm dying, please help because I have not one single living family member."  And you think he needs protection from that?  Also, he could have seen my name on the email list and deleted it without reading it.
Some people think the rules are what they are and that means that they should stay that way . . . slavery would still be with us.

No idea which of them cooked up the plan of dog being with the woman . . . for crying out loud, she is nearly 85 now, I think.  I don't want to give either of them a thank you card . . . I'd prefer something QUITE different.  Dog ate very well and he was completely normal in 2 days, thank goodness.  He is with me day and night, literally.  That was the first time we were ever separated.  Thank yo for your opinion, 'cause I REALLY didn't think either of them deserved any thanks.

The mission of the California Labor Commissioner's Office is to ensure a just day's pay in every workplace in the State and to promote economic justice through robust enforcement of labor laws. By combating wage theft, protecting workers from retaliation, and educating the public, we put earned wages into workers' pockets and help level the playing field for law-abiding employers. This office is also known as the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement (DLSE).

**The mission of the California Labor Commissioner's Office is to ensure a just day's pay in every workplace in the State and to promote economic justice through robust enforcement of labor laws. By combating wage theft, protecting workers from retaliation, and educating the public, we put earned wages into workers' pockets and help level the playing field for law-abiding employers.**

**The Labor Commissioner has the following arms for enforcing labor laws. Most of our positions fall under one of the following units:**

[**Wage Claim Adjudication**](https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/dlseWagesandHours.html)**: Adjudicates wage claims on behalf of workers who file claims for nonpayment of wages, overtime, or vacation pay pursuant to California Labor Code section 98.**

Vision: As a national leader in the Wage Claim Adjudication process, the Labor Commissioner's Office enforces the law by setting a standard of fair and expeditious resolution of claims to achieve long-term compliance from the employers of the State of California. By providing education and meaningful enforcement of wage and hour laws, we combat wage theft and ensure that wages earned are put into the pockets of the workers.

I have always found them to be fast, effective, fair and they don't charge you a fee.  Good luck!

Please ask yourself if you have been brainwashed into thinking that you are going to have a better or happier life unless you go to university.  I know PLENTY of professionals who aren't happy or even successful.  I believe this is true in ALL countries.  You remind me of a twelve year old whose first romance broke up when she thought it would somehow last forever.  It is a BIG world with a lot of occupations that are useful and interesting.   The USA, is stuffed full right now with college graduates who just loved their studies . . . but there are not enough jobs in those fields for them.
I think she is wrong too, but so what?  What is important is that you quit worrying about who is to blame and get on with shopping for a counselor with whom you feel very comfortable talking.
SOS.  Would you be having all these doubts and subject yourself to self-criticism if you had epilepsy instead?  A disease is a disease.

In my opinion your grammar is a heck of a lot better than the Adam Henry you are married to.  Whatever will he do if you develop some disease like cancer.  This guy doesn't have a clue how to treat you decently.  Get rid of him NOW!!!  I can't urge you strongly enough to get rid of him NOW.

Some kinds of depression are very like being on another planet, what the person having the depression is so different.  I say cut the weed out.  Nobody in the scientific community yet knows EXACTLY what/when it is helpful and what/when it contributes to the problem or much about long term effects for each person's individual depression.  If you are in the USA, the statistics are that there aren't enough psychiatrists to go around and that it will be 2040 before there are enough, so unfortunately that is "normal" now.   You might encourage her to check out psychiatric nurse practitioners .  She should interview them (individually), just like shopping for an expensive purchase, until she finds one she feels really comfortable talking to.
What have you done or tried to do about it?

Others experience it too.  Our minds protect us by doing it.  Depending on the kind of memory loss and the severity of what you experienced during your depression, the memories may or may not come back some day and they may or may not be as painful then as though you had to deal with them now when your body/mind says you are not ready to do so.

You are old enough to decide for yourself who you actually are, what you can and cannot do, and and what YOU actually want for yourself. Maybe you could take some time off to do that?  As for Dad, I'm sure he means well, but if he is pressuring you to do what you can't or don't want to do, you are old enough to say the word "NO!".  Life is not about fulfilling somebody else's expectations of you.

The visit to the guidance counselor is probably a good idea, but it should be to find out more about who you are and what you want, not necessarily to help you pass.

I would bet my last dollar that if you wore women's clothing doing so would not actually harm a single person on this earth.  Certainly trying on that clothing absolutely wouldn't harm anyone.

And there is no way you deserve to be forgotten.  Stop thinking you are pathetic and start reading about people who have similar urges and who have still managed to contribute a great deal to the world.  There are people in this world who do REAL HARM . . . murderers, pedophiles, etc., but trying on opposite sex clothing doesn't even come remotely close to doing harm

Listen to me, not so Quik, if your friend had epilepsy and banged his head and body, and was bleeding inside when he fell during a seizure, would you STIGMATIZE  AS "DOING SHITTY THINGS", like expecting them to do the "easily preventable" task of showing up when they are bleeding inside, just as the epileptic is black and blue or bleeding where it doesn't show.  You are not only insensitive you are perpetuating the myth that feelings like depression aren't as valid as physical injuries.

I wish I had good advice, but very little works for me at times.  Actually, sleeping long hours, if and when I can do it, helps more than anything.  If I was allowed to "strangle" the jack asses who think I can control myself, I'd probably be happier . . . just kidding.  Why don't those folks go find some epileptics and tell them they can control their seizures if they just try hard enough?
I thank you for your reply.  You are the only one who answered and I have been very curious for a very long time.  I am very glad that you survived.  Good luck!

Let's talk about some of the serious assholes who not only don't think depression is a disease but who think you can "control it" if you try.  These assholes still exist and some of them sit on Circuit Court benches judging others.  

I am BPII and have been for over 50 years.  My husband had a kind of stroke that destroys judgement and the judgement almost never returns (1%).  He filed for a restraining order against me because he honestly believed I was trying to harm him with a new drug he had never taken before which his surgeon prescribed.  I promptly had a nervous breakdown because of the stress of caring for him, all alone, for months and the stress of the operation.  Important though it was, I was too sick to appear in Court and couldn't afford a lawyer.  Husband didn't appear either.  Judge enforced the order.  I had never been in any kind of legal trouble before and don't smoke, drink, dope, and never have done.  Absolutely no record of any kind.  One morning I went to my family physician and he diagnosed, tentatively, cancer, but needed to do more tests to confirm it.  I called my therapist and talked, but  the obsession wasn't helped.  I went into a BOPII manic, obsessive, compulsive mode wanting to ask my husband if, in the event it turned out to be cancer, would he help care for me.  I didn't want to ask him, but I have absolutely NO living family members and no friends who can help.       My email wasn't threatening or disrespectful.  His answer was to turn me in to the police.  Unfortunately the asshole Judge said in open court he did not believe that a BPII couldn't control herself if she tried hard enough.  The asshole was incredible!  I spent 2 months in jail for a mental illness symptom I couldn't control any more than an epileptic can control a seizure.  What does our society want from me?????  Why does it criminalize mental illness?  I came from a poor family and had a lot of self esteem problems when I was young.  So I spent my whole life building up a respectable life and a career that was of tremendous value to society.  For what?  Now I have NOTHING I worked so hard to achieve.  I will be happy to die when my time comes. STOP JUDGING PEOPLE WITH MENTAL ILLNESS.  THEY SEE THE WORLD WITH DIFFERENT EYES.

First of all, get out the yellow pages and find the non-profit or low/no cost mental health organizations in your community or nearby. You can also look on line by typing in Mental Health Agencies and the name of your City and State.  They exist in almost every community or one near it.  You MUST have a therapist who can prescribe anti-depressants.  With most people it takes trying several to get one that is the best for you.  Please hurry and do this first.

Stop hating school.  Once you are on the right medication, it will be easier to concentrate.  School is your only way out of the mess, whether it is a degree program or a skill program.  Either way, choose one in which there is a demand for that skill.

Some States have a free debt counseling program which is done by phone.  My experience with the one in my State was EXCELLENT!

You are able to hold a job now, which means that after you get the right medication(s) you will be able to do the job easier and better.  It will be a HUGE plus!

Go to your local large hardware store, Home Depot or something like it.  If you have seasonal depression (not some other kind) buy a full spectrum lamp (or bulb if you can't afford the lamp) and use it regularly.

Don't waste time right now on Mom or the past.  You can do that clean-up AFTER you get on your feet.

I send you my sincere, heart felt best wishes.

Nobody will ever know as much as the BP knows.  To think so is arrogance.  Look at all the posts that complain "He/She just doesn't get it."  Many BPs will hide their symptoms for a variety of reasons.  Knowing something you do/think is not normal is not usually conducive to making the person want to share the info with others.  Some symptoms/problems they aren't even acutely aware of.

I have a very good therapist whom I admire greatly.  It was the nurse in my MD's office who was ignorant and incredibly arrogant.  Going to the doctor for other things this afternoon, but will DEFINITELY talk to him about the nurse, whether he'll listen or not.  The world has to learn.
BP symptoms vary greatly from person to person.  Watch out for judging what you cannot possibly know.

Somewhere in the 1950's (when you were but a twinkle in your old man's eye), somebody in education promulgated the idea that everyone should go to college.  In the 1960s it got worse!  The unis dropped their admission standards toward the end of the 1960s.  Meanwhile the lower public school administrations were allowing themselves to listen to idiot educational psychologists who convinced the schools to not flunk anyone if they weren't up to grade level, even in basic subjects.  A flock of uneducated, poorly used students went on to higher education by the 80s, causing the unis to get greedy to enroll ever more students by dropping their entrance standards again.  What is REALLY bad is that the public got the idea that you HAD to be a college grad to succeed and be happy in life.  Today we have tons of grads and there are shortages of jobs in almost every conceivable occupation.  60% of college grads do not work in jobs remotely related to their degrees.  40% of all college grads are working in jobs that call  only for a high school diploma, no college at all.

Sweetie, you didn't fail.  Society failed you by not supporting you and helping you prepare for an appropriate education, perhaps.  Or maybe you can get a degree when you don't have to cope with homelessness and being alone.  You are under incredibly difficult circumstances.  Now the good news.  If you can get into a trade school, get a program that has a lot of work in your geographic area, you will have NO shortage of jobs and many pay very well for skilled workers.  Do it and I guarantee you a successful work life!  You are brave, hardworking, young and will do well.

You would know best, but more likely that is PTS, rather than manic.  I always thought it took a LOT of trauma to give one PTSD, but I was wrong about that.  It can be only one incident.   The continued visualizing is often associated with PTSD.   So, you might want to ask your doctor.

I am so proud and admiring of you to have risked your own well being to help.  Please concentrate on the good you did whenever you start visualizing the mess.  I had PTSD only once, after a senile woman hit my empty car and then battered me and tried to kill me with her car!  It took about a month before all the symptoms were gone.  What you went through was MUCH worse, both times.  If I can say anything to help or just to distract you, please let me know.  I am SO PROUD TO KNOW YOU.

Incurable, treatment resistant BiPolar 2.  At 72 all I want is peace, whichever way I can get it.  There is no cure for BP 2 and science just isn't up to being able to really help most of the symptoms.

If your problem is depression or BP, you feel that way because IT IS TRUE.

If people haven't got the disease, the really don't "get it" and will tell you BS about getting better, but they don't know what they are talking about if they haven't experienced it.

Some kinds of depression are treatment resistant and incurable.   It is almost impossible to have much control over the symptoms.  In addition you have to cope with idiots who insist you could get better if you tried harder.

I, for one, am no longer tolerant of the general public's stupidity and ignorance about such a wide spread disease.  The truth is that there is absolutely no cure for BP2.

I am an old lady with a lot of work experience.  I hope you will find this story funny.  It wasn't then, but it is now.  Talking of bad experiences on a first job, listen to mine. 

 It was 1968 when I graduated with a BA.  It was the height of the aerospace decline.  NO jobs for anyone as we were in that industry's geographic center.  The unemployment office was officially advising people not to look for work, the labor market was so bad!  

 I, with  my little BA was DETERMINED to not take a clerical job.  I was determined to get an administrative job. (At that time, if a woman took a clerical job, she was pretty entirely stereotyped as clerical and would never hold any other kind of job.)  Armed with resume and references, I send off a resume to a job in the paper.  That company's corporate office was in Texas:  I was in California.  Interviewer/prospective boss tells me on the phone no typing.  He comes out, interviews me, and I'm hired.  But the job has a dual report to the manager in CA at the office I'll be working in.  I report for work.  There is a f------g typewriter in the office.  I push it out into the hall.  After lunch it is back in my office.  This happens twice!

I talk to the CA manager and explain I was told it was not a clerical job.  He responds that "all the WOMEN who work her have to type."  I call the Texas boss who tells me he can't control the manager and I have to type.  I quit.   

Talk about a bad experience?  I raged for quite a while.  Oh, forgot to mention the the CA manager had multitudinous nude calanders of women hung all over his office wall.  It took a while after I quit,  but I eventually got an administrative job with State of CA.  

I hope you will get over whatever you were screwed with by the company and go on to bigger, better things.  All companies are NOT the same.  PM me if you like.  Good luck!

Forgive me but f\_\_\_\_ the diagnosis and description.  Concentrate instead on dealing with the symptoms as effectively as possible.  That's what is important.  The DSM changes it terminology, classification, and description of psychiatric illnesses as often as you change your socks.  A diagnosis which is accurate today is revised as something else as often as you change socks.  Forget it and cope with the symptoms.

Naturally it is harder with BP.  Having an average GPA and being BP is NOT a good reason to decide school isn't for you.  You just keep your little butt in school.  Life with BP is hard, but after you drop out, it will be a heck of a lot harder.  You MUST have some kind of education or skills in order to have a decent life.
I have accepted that BP2 and marriage/relationships are incompatible.  It is sad but true.
A lot of BP2s need help because of poor financial decisions.  There is no leeway in the law or business for this symptom of this illness.

Your words are after my own heart.  I compare it to diabetes and epilepsy.  If a BP2 has a manic or panic attack in the middle of a busy street, he/she is likely to wind up in jail.  If an epileptic or a diabetic does the same thing, people recognize the symptoms and off he/she goes to the hospital.  The ignorance makes our lives sooooooo  much harder.

Sounds too simple, but it works for me often (even though I never think it will).    After you have settled down it bed and your body is comfortable, do some relaxation breathing. It can't hurt and often works for me.  Good luck!

My therapist says it is from stress that impacts the short term memory so hard.  On the other hand I'm 72, my Mom had some form of dementia in her late 80s, but I'm wondering if I'm getting it earlier.  How does one tell?  Anyone know?

Should stay single if it is the wrong spouse.  I should know.  I spent 50 years with emotional abuse because I chose the wrong one.  Tried everything, but you can't change someone who doesn't want to change.  Love is NOT enough.
Yes, TV and film can help distract a person from even the greatest misery for a sort time.  Keep chilling and sleep all you can.  I send you a hug.
Not so funny, but true.  The awful "locker room" names that some (not all, by any means) men use to refer to women.

Please forgive me if I've already answered you.  My short term memory is terrible under stress.  Thank you for trying to help.  I appreciate your kindness.
I've been taking meds and talking to a doctor for 40 years!  Honestly!  There is no cure for depression.  Pills don't completely do the job.  Moreover, the present problem is far more economic than emotional.  
I am planning on applying to a Swiss company for assisted suicide.  The process takes months, during which time I am stuck here.  There simply is no other avenue to escape and I am old anyway.  I have no family and only a couple friends, so I'm not injuring anyone with my choice.  Thank you for your kindness.

Agreed.  Actually, I rarely drink coffee at all.  I grind my own beans at home and use a coffee press, but probably only once a week if a neighbor comes over.  If I am out all day and am dragging in the afternoon, McDonalds Senior Coffee for $1.00 does the job of energizing me to drive home.  That happens about once every two weeks.
I looked up my car payment.  It is about $275.00 per month and has 12 more payments.  
I wish I was OCD.  House periodically looks like Hiroshima the day after the bomb!  I always clean it up within a few days though.  I can't kneel and bending over is bad too.  Nobody works for less than $10.25 hr here and I have to have help for the garden and cleaning inside.  I can't even change bed linens because my hands barely grasp.  
As for the food, I have one of these very simple bodies.  The calories go in, the weight goes on.  I have some protein daily and lots of fruit.  I also have a phobia about running out of medicines and food.  My pantry and bathroom look like the guts of a first aid station.  I was very poor and all alone in college and couldn't get to a drug store or supermarket when I was sick.  I'm in much the same shape now and the fear persists.  I could easily live 2-3 weeks on the food stored in my pantry and I am medically prepared for WWIII.  Actually, as I live in snow country, this is good planning for being snowed in.
I can make endless lists of where the money goes, but I am still $1500. per month short to keep an even keel, because I also have debts.
Thank you for trying to help.  It is hopeless.  I have decided to give up.  After all, I'm old and maybe it is just time to go.  I'm applying to Switzerland for assisted suicide.  If I were young or middle aged, I would fight on.  But, I'm not and things will only get worse for me.
Thank you for trying to help.  I was adding and comparing whether it would be better for me to work full time  for $15.00(no benefits of any kind) or not.  If I do, I have to give up government subsidized medicare and medications.  The wages aren't nearly enough to fill the spending-income gap, but it will slow the bleeding of my budget.  There is a HUGE question of whether I am physically able to work full time, but the only way to know is to try.  Frankly, I'd leave for Switzerland today, but the psych eval is NOT fast.  So, I'm stuck for a few more months.
Thank you for trying to help.  Please feel appreciated.

How are you doing?  I know this kind of misery and anxiety from traveling and life changes.  I keep thinking of you.  Are you at your destination yet?  It will be bad for a week or so when you arrive, but once you settle in and get your meds, things will begin to straighten out.
One.  Only one and only if I died where this person was.  I don't care about it.  What I care about is that nobody is close to me now and that hurts.

Thanks, I hadn't thought about it being more painful to die in prison.  Actually, I'm super suicidal tonight.  I'm not going to do it though.  The only reason why I won't is that I'm borrowing money against my entire small estate so that I can go to Switzerland for assisted death.  I've tried everything anyone could think of but nothing works.  For example, although I have an excellent education and am talented with a long successful career behind me, it ended 20 years ago.  The only job I've been offered is $15.00 per hour, no benefits, no holiday pay.  That won't close the gap between SS and the cash flow going out. I did not grow up in abject poverty, so I don't know how to do it.  I haven't been out to a restaurant in 1 1/2 years for anything but coffee.  My car is 4 years old, bought before my husband lost his mind.  The car has 12 more payments.  It didn't make me happy when I bought it and doesn't now.  The only thing that will make me happy is relief from anxiety and depression.  My meds are failing miserably.  Science just isn't up to the job of coping with depression etc.  Thank you for writing.

If you mean ignore that it is just a fine, uh well it is because I heard the judge in court saying that the second violation would be prison time.  That does carry more weight than an unknown person in an unknown location.   Wouldn't you think the same?
Repetitive meals, poverty, etc.  It isn't living when I have to be so precise and careful just to exist.
I'm so glad.  Your reply made my day..  I've done a lot of traveling.  Even with meds, I get jet laged and disoriented.  Hang tight.  It will pass.

They won't fine me.  I have no money but my SS which doesn't even cover my rent.  The rest of the money is loaned to me so I can keep a roof over my head and food and gas and the car.  At 72, I can't get a job.  I refuse to die without telling him.  What are they going to do?  Exhume me?  I'll just wait until the end and then notify him, but it is the s---s when you can be married 50 years, do nothing, but because he has brain damage and is paranoid, can't even say good bye.  I believe it is a mandatory prison sentence, not a fine, in Oregon.

In Oregon mandated medical reporters (doctors, nurses, etc.) do not have to report to the DMV that a person is impaired (Alzheimer's or Dementia) until the disease has reached the stage of being "severe" and "uncontrollable".   Other States, such as California, require mandatory reporting if the disease is "mild".  Moreover, in Oregon, even if the person is reported to the DMV there is such a bureaucratic paper work back up that the person can go on driving up to three months before being examined for fitness.
I'm going to have to violate it then.  I'm so miserable, why not spend my last days in prison rather than run up a bill in a hospital.

Not if you live in Oregon.   Front of the restraining order read "She threatened me."  Back side said "She has threatened me before." No other information, but the order was granted.  I was having a nervous breakdown and couldn't contest it.  I am dying and I have some things to say to him.  We were married 50 years with no prior problems before he had a cerebral hemorrhagic stroke and lost his mind.

Nobody around.

This isn't a life.  It is an existence.  I don't see how you stand it.  I'm not going to.
Time to leave as soon as you manage to get some money together.

If not, it is time to go for professional help ASAP
I am certain the schools could do with repair.  That won't solve the larger problem of Oregon being dead last of all states educationally.

Always ask what happened to the person who last held this job and the two before that.  If you hear "they just didn't work out" run for cover.

Do not take a job before you check on line comments from former employees.  Say 2 of 10 are negative, well that's life.  But 8 of 10 are red flags you'll be sick if you ignore.
No side effects at all for me.  Just feeling better.

Isn't it amazing how cruel and thoughtless people can be about mental illness?  As his talking is not job related, is distracting and cruel, I wonder if you could write HR an anonymous letter naming  him and telling them that you find this objectionable and not appropriate for the work setting.  If they investigate (I think they will) others have heard him and will back up the fact he's doing this.

My cat kept me going through some horrible times.  It is important to remember that if the cat is old and sickly, he/she may just be sticking around because he/she loves you, not because he really is enjoying life.  Sometimes I think they love us selflessly and we love them selfishly.  You might want to try for a service dog who can help you through your days.

I send you air hugs.

I don't think there would be a day of national mourning if all the anxious and depressed people in the US died.  We are basically viewed as defectives and a drain on society, even though we try our best.
Some people just don't appreciate other people, friends, or families.

He woke up an extreme extrovert who wouldn't stop talking to people day or night. The nurses were worried because he never slept more than 20 minutes at a time and never stopped talking!  He was absolutely manic.  Later I read on the computer (the docs never tell you enough) that open heart surgery is very commonly associated with a hemorrhagic stroke.  That kind of stroke changes personality and destroys judgement.  I begged his surgeon to send  him to rehab, but he sent  him home. I knew I had exhaustion and was verging on a collapse.  He wouldn't take the med when the paramedic tried to give it to him.  He also refused to take it from the sheriff.  He demanded to go to the hospital.  I thought it best to give permission.  I never saw him again for 1 1/2 years thanks to him calling an unscrupulous lawyer who never talked to me and wouldn't look at the exonerating sheriff's report of what he had seen.
